It uses obfuscation, hidden directories, and scheduled tasks to evade detection and maintain persistence, posing a severe risk to users.

behavioral_signatures: Creation and execution of files in hidden directories (e.g., ~/.local/bin/vscode)
Downloading and executing remote scripts or executables at runtime
Creation of scheduled tasks for persistence (e.g., chromeUpdate)
Access and exfiltration of AWS credentials via HTTP POST
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to 89.44.9.227 with AWS credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated URL construction and outbound HTTP requests to suspicious IPs (e.g., 89.44.9.227). Flag creation or execution of files in hidden directories (such as ~/.local/bin/vscode) or the Downloads folder, especially scripts or executables. Detect scheduled tasks named 'chromeUpdate' or similar, and alert on any process that accesses AWS credentials and sends them externally. Use static analysis to identify platform-detecting code that dispatches OS-specific payloads.
